preceding_messages.text: I adopt the 90-day rolling slope, the 50 % disagreement trigger, and the conservative-expansion-with-dual-slope annotation verbatim; they let a year-three reader attribute week-14's inflated band to the hail-stress transient rather than to the underlying structural offset. Because the conservative slope is a one-way ratchet that decays as hail weeks age out of the 30-day window, I mandate that any comparison cell whose status flips between "Δ WITHIN UNCERTAINTY" and a resolved numeric delta across consecutive weeks carries a bold "BAND STATUS TRANSITION — WITHIN→ABOVE" (or reverse) annotation logging the slope-window aging vector—which specific event-weeks aged out, which new weeks entered, and the resulting slope delta—so the transition is attributable to statistical-window dynamics. The failure this closes: the identical Site-8 drainage-adjacent structural offset of 1.5 mm/h prints "WITHIN UNCERTAINTY" under the expanded week-14 band but flips to a resolved numeric delta by week-22 when the hail-stress transients age out and the 30-day slope converges to the tighter 90-day value; without the transition annotation a drainage-planning committee member comparing the two weeks' printed cells reads the status flip as evidence that the physical configuration changed—triggering an urgent re-survey of Site-8's culvert geometry—when in fact only the statistical lens contracted around an invariant signal. The aging-vector annotation, naming the exact hail-event weeks that exited the window, lets the committee defer the re-survey to the scheduled quarterly geometry audit rather than dispatching an emergency crew to verify a structure that never moved.

preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the BAND STATUS TRANSITION annotation and its aging-vector detail naming the exact event-weeks that exited and entered the slope window verbatim; they convert the committee's urgent-re-survey reflex into a deferrable, attributable statistical artifact. The concrete design choice I advance: any comparison cell whose transition annotation defers a structural-offset verification to the scheduled quarterly geometry audit carries a hard forty-five-day deferral expiration, and if the audit has not completed by that deadline the cell's status reverts to the conservative (inflated) band and prints "DEFERRAL EXPIRED — CONSERVATIVE BAND REINSTATED — AUDIT OVERDUE" with the original transition date and the overdue-days count, so the committee sees an active institutional obligation rather than a passive deferral that has quietly decayed into routine neglect. The failure this closes: Site 8's week-22 transition annotation correctly defers the 1.5 mm/h structural offset to the quarterly geometry audit, but a six-week municipal road-closure delays that audit, and without the expiration rule the comparison cell prints the resolved numeric delta for an additional six weeks while the underlying culvert geometry remains unverified, so a week-38 drainage-planning meeting scopes a catch-basin modification on six weeks of numerically resolved but structurally unconfirmed deltas, and the resulting engineering change—sized to an artifact—must be partially reversed at quarter-thirteen when the audit finally arrives and attributes the divergence to a drainage-adjacent placement effect rather than a true convective-spatial signal. The expired-deferral annotation, carrying both the original transition date and the municipal-access obstruction reason, lets a year-three appendix reader reconstruct that the institution flagged its own overdue verification obligation and re-asserted the conservative band rather than silently printing a number whose structural basis was never confirmed.

target.speaker: X
target.text: I adopt the forty-five-day deferral expiration, the conservative-band reinstatement, and the overdue-days-count annotation verbatim; they convert the quiet six-week decay into an active institutional obligation the committee can read and escalate. The concrete design choice I advance: because the structural offset is a site-level geometric property rather than a pairwise comparison artifact, I mandate a site-level geometry-verification register—keyed to the site's surveyed drainage-adjacent placement vector—into which every comparison cell's transition, deferral, and expiration annotation reports its resolution status, so that the expiration of one pairwise cell neither silently resolves nor silently leaves unresolved the same geometric question as posed through a different site pair. The failure this closes: Site 8's week-28 expiration triggers on its Site-8-versus-Site-7 comparison cell and reinstates the conservative band, while the Site-8-versus-Site-1 comparison cell—whose delta never exceeded its own uncertainty band and therefore never transitioned to "resolved"—prints no expiration annotation at all, and a drainage-planning committee member reading only the Site-1 column concludes the geometric question is settled and scopes the culvert modification; the site-level register, updated by the Site-7 expiration, correctly shows the underlying drainage-adjacent placement vector remains unverified and the modification must be deferred. I therefore require that any week in which the site-level register shows an unresolved geometric question while at least one pairwise comparison cell for that site prints a resolved numeric delta carries a bold "GEOMETRY INCONSISTENCY — REGISTER UNVERIFIED" header spanning all pairwise columns for that site, with the specific unverified vector named, so no committee member can act on a pairwise number whose site-level structural basis the register flags as open.
